replication.target_description: Likely-GAD subgroup main effect of face valence on reaction times, follow-up ANOVA at p.726. Source identifies faster angry-versus-neutral responses in GAD as the specific replication claim; no numeric pairwise statistic is printed.

n.sample_role: participants meeting likely GAD criteria, subgroup used in face-valence follow-up
n.exclusions: From 139 tested, 6 excluded for incomplete/missing data; 133 retained overall (63 GAD, 29 HTA, 41 control). Incorrect responses and time outlier trials excluded.

None of the ﬁndings reported by Yiend and colleagues

notes: Retains published volume year 2023 and DOI/publication copyright 2024. Rendered p.726 checked: unusual printed η² < .000 retained verbatim without correction. Requested etasq is reported for the GAD face-valence omnibus, while the exact angry-versus-neutral post hoc contrast has only a nonsignificance statement and no numeric p/effect. No p inferred or calculated. Overall 3×3 interaction is a different test (partial η² < .000). Explicit ellipses omit interleaved opposite-column table/prose in canonical TXT.
